payload.summary: Added `featuresDir` to the config and a new `src/features/` module: a feature schema, a regex-based Mermaid node scanner and `loadFeatureMap`, which reads the map README and the feature docs into a typed model and reports what it can't parse as problems.
payload.commitMessage: feat(features): feature map loader with config, frontmatter schema and mermaid nodes
notes: src/features/featureSchema.ts: FEATURE_ID_PATTERN (`<area>/<name>` kebab), FEATURE_ID_PART_PATTERN, FeatureFrontmatterSchema (strict; depends_on/tests/specs default [], code min 1, glob chars rejected in code/tests), type FeatureFrontmatter, nodeIdOf(id), REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ['Purpose','Capabilities','Expectations'], OPTIONAL_SECTIONS = ['Pitfalls','Out of scope'] (readonly tuples).

src/features/mermaidNodes.ts: mermaidBlocks(markdown): string[] (contents of ```mermaid fences), definedNodes(block): string[] (unique, in order of first definition; skips label text, |edge labels| and the ignored keyword lines).

src/features/loadFeatureMap.ts: loadFeatureMap(repoRoot, config): FeatureMap | null, which returns null when <featuresDir> is missing or not a directory. Also exports FEATURE_MAP_FILE = 'README.md' and the types Problem, FeatureIndexRow, FeatureMapReadme, FeatureDoc and FeatureMap.

FeatureMap.readme: { path, mermaidBlocks (count), nodes (unique across all blocks), rows: { id, link: string | null, title }[] } | null. `link` is null when the ID cell is not a `[id](link)` link, and then `id` is the raw cell text.
All paths (readme.path, doc.path, problem.path) are repo-relative and use `/`, e.g. `docs/features/board/turns.md`. Docs are sorted by path.

FeatureDoc: { path, idFromPath (`<area>/<name>`, not validated), frontmatter | null, sections (H2 headings in document order, fenced code ignored), capabilities (top-level `- ` lines of ## Capabilities) }.

Problems the loader emits, each { path, message, level }: missing frontmatter, invalid frontmatter YAML and schema violations (all errors on the doc path); README without a `## Features` section (error); malformed table rows with fewer than 3 cells (error); .md files at other depths than <area>/<name>.md (warning). FM-2 should not report these again.

FM-2 still has to check: id vs path, ID pattern, the mermaid block count being exactly 1, rows vs docs, nodes vs features, node collisions, section order and required sections, and that depends_on and code/tests paths exist.

deviations.what: I changed the existing 'fills every default for a minimal config' test in configSchema.spec.ts to expect `featuresDir: 'docs/features'`.
deviations.why: The test compares the whole parsed config with toEqual, so a new default field makes it fail unless the expectation includes it. Leaving existing config tests unchanged was not possible.

deviations.what: The loader also reports a README without a `## Features` section as an error, and table rows with fewer than 3 cells as errors.
deviations.why: Without these problems the check could not tell a missing table from an empty one, and malformed rows would be dropped silently. Both count as 'reports what it can't parse'.

deviations.what: Markdown files at other depths than <area>/<name>.md are reported as warnings and are not loaded as docs.
deviations.why: The brief says 'other depths reported' but does not give a level.

question.text: Which level should a .md file at the wrong depth under featuresDir get?

deviations.what: `code`/`tests` entries that contain glob characters (*?[]{}) fail the frontmatter schema.
deviations.why: FMD-4 says 'no globs'. It does not say whether the schema enforces this or the check does.

question.text: Should the frontmatter schema reject glob patterns in code/tests, or leave it to the existence check?
